name: Muelle de las Almas, Chiloé
why: Through Chilote forest and pasture to the cliffs of Punta Pirulil, where a wooden pier rises over the Pacific for the souls waiting for the boatman Tempilkawe.
book: Private land: pay the entry (CLP 10,000 in Wikipedia) at the kiosk on the road from Cucao towards Rahue, then drive about 8 km to the private car park. In summer the queue for a photo on the pier can be hours long: come early.
water: Nothing to buy after the car park: carry water and food.
dangers: Mud on the path after rain, which is often.
Wind and wet on the cliff top: stay behind the fences at Punta Pirulil.
The gravel road from Cucao gets bad in rain.
turnaround: Not at the pier one hour after leaving the car park: turn back, the path and the road are worse in the dark and the rain.

points.name: Muelle de las Almas car park, Rahue
points.note: The private car park at the end of the road; the path leaves west through forest and fields towards the sea.

points.name: Muelle de las Almas, Punta Pirulil
points.note: Marcelo Orellana's wooden pier climbs into the air off the Pirulil cliffs, where souls call the ferryman Tempilkawe in Chilote legend. Back the same way.
